thread:
SRE-Bot: ALERT: 4 nodes in cluster inference-pool-usw changed to NotReady over the last 3m. firing: k8s_node_notready (severity=critical)
Ashish Rao: paging oncall — I'm seeing the alert, checking. 4 nodes NotReady, some pods evicted. @Maya can you pick this up?
Maya Patel: on it. pulling up dashboards. are customers seeing errors?
Jun Park: metrics: 90th latency for /v1/generate up from 120ms -> 800ms. 503 rate at ~1.2% for last 5m. error logs show a lot of `context deadline exceeded` and `rpc error: code = Unavailable`.
Carla Mendes: hmm that lines up with kubelet churn; if nodes are flapping the load balancer might be retrying and hitting fallback routes. any kubelet logs?
Ashish Rao: grabbing `kubectl get nodes -l pool=inference-usw -o wide` now.
Ashish Rao: ```
NAME                          STATUS     ROLES    AGE    VERSION
infer-node-17                 NotReady   <none>   42d    v1.27.3
infer-node-21                 Ready      <none>   11d    v1.27.3
infer-node-23                 NotReady   <none>   3d     v1.27.3
infer-node-29                 NotReady   <none>   2d     v1.27.3
infer-node-34                 Ready      <none>   5h     v1.27.3
```
Maya Patel: node age spread suggests a couple newer nodes as well. can someone `kubectl describe node infer-node-17` and paste kubelet restart count?
Jun Park: pasted relevant section from `journalctl -u kubelet -n 200` on infer-node-17: ```
-- Logs begin at ...
Mar 15 03:14:27 infer-node-17 kubelet[1234]: E0315 03:14:27 kubelet_pods.go:123] failed to sync pod "lr-infer-abc-7f6df": runtime service error: timed out
Mar 15 03:14:28 infer-node-17 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
Mar 15 03:14:29 infer-node-17 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Failed with result 'exit-code'.
Mar 15 03:14:30 infer-node-17 systemd[1]: kubelet.service: Started kubelet.
```
Carla Mendes: that matches a pattern of kubelet crashing, not just kube-proxy flapping. could be driver/kernel OOM or kubelet segfault on node. any GPU driver errors?
Ashish Rao: checking dmesg snippet from node-17: ```
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=10321, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[  123.456799] Kernel panic - not syncing: GPU driver timeout
```
Maya Patel: oh that's bad — GPU driver instability. likely a CUDA/NVIDIA driver issue causing processes to panic and kubelet to restart. impacted nodes are those with recent driver updates.
SRE-Bot: PagerDuty: page created for oncall @pager oncall.
PagerDuty: Pager sent to "sre-oncall" (Maya Patel).
Maya Patel: plan: 1) cordon and drain the 3 NotReady/unstable nodes to evacuate workloads to healthy nodes/pools, 2) scale up Dedicated fallback nodes (inference-fallback pool) by +3 while we rotate, 3) restart kubelet + GPU driver on affected nodes when safe, 4) route traffic away from drained nodes. executing now.
Ashish Rao: I'm running cordon/drain on infer-node-17 and infer-node-23. commands: ```
kubectl cordon infer-node-17
kubectl drain infer-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```
Jun Park: starting scale on dedicated fallback: `kubectl scale --replicas=12 deploy/realtime-infer-fallback -n inference` -> +3 replicas.
Carla Mendes: adding temporary LB weight shift to prefer inference-fallback region-usw-2 (manual route rule set). Can we enable automatic fallback for the route?
Ashish Rao: adding annotation to service: `redwood.io/prefer-fallback: true` so console routing will route requests to fallback variant for new requests.
Maya Patel: nodes drained. one node (infer-node-29) still showing kubelet restart loop. I'm going to reboot that host via infra runbook (soft reboot) to ensure driver unload. @Carla can you coordinate with infra to hold off any disruptive infra upgrades?
Carla Mendes: pinged infra, removing scheduled driver upgrades in the region for next 24h.
Ops-Bot: deploy-bot: scaled realtime-infer-fallback to 12 replicas — rollout in progress.
Jun Park: fallback capacity is up, traffic shift looks good. 95th latency falling back to ~160ms, 503s down to 0.15%. still seeing occasional client retries but steady.
Maya Patel: summary so far: root cause appears to be an NVIDIA driver regression on a subset of hosts causing GPU to 'fall off bus' -> kernel/GPU faults -> kubelet exits -> node NotReady -> pod evictions -> increased latency and 503s. mitigation: drained unstable nodes, scaled fallback pool, routed traffic away, infra rebooted one host.
Ashish Rao: we're going to rotate the remaining unstable nodes out of the pool and mark them for driver rollback. creating an infra ticket to revert driver to 535.86.05 which was stable last week.
Jun Park: creating temporary alert to suppress noisy node flapping pages and surface the underlying driver errors only: silencing k8s_node_notready for inference-pool-usw where we've got active rotation.
Maya Patel: next steps: - infra to rollback driver and run soak; - SRE to add kubelet-restart-rate alert (>=3 restarts in 5m) and Nvidia XID pattern alert; - product/contact teams: notify customers who hit errors (ops->eng-sre will draft msg).
Carla Mendes: filing incident ticket and will attach timeline + actions. I'll prepare the postmortem template.
Ashish Rao: current status: all traffic healthy, fallback serving ~12% of inference volume in region, nodes being rotated. leaving thread open for 2hr monitoring.
PagerDuty: Incident status: acknowledged -> mitigated (auto).
Maya Patel: thanks team. leaving a short checklist for the postmortem: (1) driver rollback schedule + verification plan, (2) add node labeling to prevent staged upgrades during high traffic, (3) improve eviction/routing graceful window, (4) customer follow-up.
Ashish Rao: noted. closing out once infra confirms driver rollback and nodes stable for 30m. :white_check_mark:
Carla Mendes: thank you all — great quick coordination. :raised_hands:
